purpose: The cite-only registry. Authoring agents may cite ONLY claims marked citable=true. Anything else must appear in the blueprint as UNVERIFIED - REQUIRES CONFIRMATION or not at all.

claims.claim_text: The project definition is the framework object under which every other project object is created.
claims.evidence_quote: The project definition is a framework for all the objects created within a project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The project definition is a framework for all the objects created within a project."
claims.notes: Tier-2 product-behaviour statement; acceptable at this tier.

claims.claim_text: A project definition must exist before any WBS can be created; it is the mandatory first object.
claims.evidence_quote: Before you create a WBS, you have to create a project definition.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Before you create a WBS, you have to create a project definition." Confirmed verbatim on a second targeted exact-string pass.
claims.notes: First re-fetch returned a paraphrase; a second exact-string pass confirmed the sentence is verbatim.

claims.claim_text: Project definition holds project-wide data such as start/finish dates, organizational data and planning parameters.
claims.evidence_quote: The project definition contains data that affects the entire project (for example, start and finish dates, organizational data, and planning parameters).
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The project definition contains data that affects the entire project (for example, start and finish dates, organizational data, and planning parameters)."
claims.notes: Confirmed verbatim on second exact-string pass.

claims.claim_text: Project definition values act as defaults that are pushed down to WBS elements.
claims.evidence_quote: It contains default values that can be passed on to the WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "It contains default values that can be passed on to the WBS elements."
claims.notes: Source says values CAN be passed on, not that they always are. Corroborated more strongly by Tier-1 record R01-008.

claims.claim_text: Controlling area is fixed at project definition level and is unique for the whole project.
claims.evidence_quote: The controlling area that you specify when you create a project definition is unique for the entire project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The controlling area that you specify when you create a project definition is unique for the entire project."
claims.notes: Independently corroborated by Tier-1 source of R01-006.

claims.claim_text: Controlling area cannot be overridden on an individual WBS element.
claims.evidence_quote: The project definition's controlling area is valid for the entire project and cannot be changed for a WBS element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The project definition's controlling area is valid for the entire project and cannot be changed for a WBS element."
claims.notes: Classic on-premise PS page (Organizational Data). Scope is correct as stated.

claims.claim_text: Plant, company code and business area may differ per WBS element even inside one project.
claims.evidence_quote: You can assign different plants, company codes, and business areas to WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "You can assign different plants, company codes, and business areas to WBS elements." The same page adds that profit center, object class, change number and currency are also assignable per WBS element, and that WBS currency is changeable only until currency-dependent data is saved.
claims.notes: The currency-lock rule on the same page is a useful additional constraint the lane did not capture.

claims.claim_text: On creation or insertion, a WBS element copies organizational values down from the project definition.
claims.evidence_quote: When you create new WBS elements or incorporate them into a WBS, the values from the project definition are copied into the WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "When you create new WBS elements or incorporate them into a WBS, the values from the project definition are copied into the WBS elements."

claims.claim_text: The WBS is a hierarchical model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy.
claims.evidence_quote: The work breakdown structure (WBS) is a model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The work breakdown structure (WBS) is a model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy."

claims.claim_text: The WBS is the functional basis for downstream planning: process, cost, scheduling, capacity planning and costing.
claims.evidence_quote: the functional basis for further planning steps in a project, for example, for process planning, cost planning, scheduling, capacity planning or costing.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "the functional basis for further planning steps in a project, for example, for process planning, cost planning, scheduling, capacity planning or costing"

claims.claim_text: A WBS element is the structure element of the WBS and describes a task or a further-divisible partial task.
claims.evidence_quote: Structure element of the work breakdown structure (WBS). A WBS element describes either a certain task or a partial task that can be subdivided further.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Structure element of the work breakdown structure (WBS). A WBS element describes either a certain task or a partial task that can be subdivided further." The page also notes (DIN 69 901) that a work package can be represented by either a WBS element or an activity.
claims.notes: The DIN 69 901 note - a work package may be EITHER a WBS element OR an activity - is material to any WBS-to-Zoho mapping and was not captured in the lane.

claims.claim_text: WBS elements may be subdivided across arbitrarily many levels until the required level of detail is reached.
claims.evidence_quote: You can divide these WBS elements at various levels until you reach the level of detail you require.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "You can divide these WBS elements at various levels until you reach the level of detail you require."
claims.notes: Source says 'at various levels', which does NOT assert 'arbitrarily many levels' as the claim_text words it. No level ceiling is stated either way; the lane's gap note on this is correct.

claims.claim_text: Because the WBS is hierarchical, values summarize upward and are displayed on higher-level WBS elements.
claims.evidence_quote: Since the WBS is structured hierarchically, the data can be summarized and displayed at the corresponding higher-level WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Since the WBS is structured hierarchically, the data can be summarized and displayed at the corresponding higher-level WBS elements."
claims.notes: Source says data CAN be summarized; the claim's 'values summarize upward' reads as automatic. Minor.

claims.claim_text: Project hierarchies exist to aggregate data, allocate budget and define responsibility.
claims.evidence_quote: Hierarchies are often used for the following purposes: Evaluating aggregated data, Allocating budgets, Defining responsibilities
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Evaluating aggregated data, Allocating budgets, Defining responsibilities"

claims.claim_text: The WBS aggregates dates, costs and commitments coming from network activities.
claims.evidence_quote: The work breakdown structure can be used to aggregate dates, costs, and commitments from the network activities.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The work breakdown structure can be used to aggregate dates, costs, and commitments from the network activities."

claims.claim_text: Revenue planning/actuals and budgeting sit on WBS elements, not on network activities.
claims.evidence_quote: The WBS elements themselves would be used for planned and actual revenues, and they can also be used for budgeting, if required.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The page states only what WBS elements ARE used for. It makes NO negative statement that revenue cannot be planned or posted on network activities. It also qualifies budgeting with 'if required', which the lane's quote silently dropped, along with the leading 'The'.
claims.notes: HIGH IMPACT. The claim_text's exclusive clause 'not on network activities' is the researcher's inference, not the source's statement. A Zoho data model that hard-forbids revenue on activity-level objects would be resting on unsourced text. Narrower true statement: WBS elements are used for planned and actual revenues and may optionally be used for budgeting.

claims.claim_text: Creating a WBS requires entering a project profile for the project.
claims.evidence_quote: When you create a work breakdown structure, you must also enter a project profile for the project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "When you create a work breakdown structure, you must also enter a project profile for the project."

claims.claim_text: The project profile supplies default values and processing parameters such as settlement schema and factory calendar.
claims.evidence_quote: The project profile contains default values and parameters for processing the project, for example, which settlement schema is valid
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: "The project profile contains default values and parameters for processing the project, for example, which settlement schema is valid, which factory calendar is used for time scheduling, or which settings are used for graphics."
claims.notes: Claim's mention of factory calendar is supported by the full sentence, which the lane's quote truncated before.

claims.claim_text: The chosen project profile is stored on the project definition once the WBS is created.
claims.evidence_quote: If you create a work breakdown structure, the project profile is saved in the project definition.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "If you create a work breakdown structure, the project profile is saved in the project definition." The page adds: "You can change default settings from the project profile when you are working with the work breakdown structure."
claims.notes: The overridability sentence is important and was not captured: profile values are defaults, not locks.

claims.claim_text: A project carries exactly one project profile; the profile type drives accounting behaviour.
claims.evidence_quote: There can only be one project profile per project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "There can only be one project profile per project." Preceded by: "In the project financial control process, you use project profiles to differentiate between accounting scenarios. The type of project profile influences a project's behavior with default information."
claims.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. SCOPE CAVEAT: this is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The four-way accounting typology on this page (Overhead / Investment / Statistical / Project with Revenue) is Cloud-specific. The one-profile-per-project half is independently corroborated for classic PS by the Tier-1 source of R01-019.

claims.claim_text: Coding masks exist to render and structure complex project numbers for display and entry.
claims.evidence_quote: Coding masks serve as a display option for complex project numbers.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Coding masks serve as a display option for complex project numbers."

claims.claim_text: Mask syntax uses X for alphanumeric positions and 0 for numeric positions, plus special characters as separators.
claims.evidence_quote: The following characters are available for editing and structuring project numbers: X for alphanumeric characters, and 0 for numeric characters and special characters.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The following characters are available for editing and structuring project numbers: X for alphanumeric characters, and 0 for numeric characters and special characters."
claims.notes: The source sentence is itself ambiguously punctuated ('0 for numeric characters and special characters'); the claim's reading (X=alphanumeric, 0=numeric, plus separators) is the sensible one but the source does not cleanly separate the third category.

claims.claim_text: The mask that applies is selected by the leading characters of the project number, which act as the coding key.
claims.evidence_quote: The way it is set up depends on the first characters of the project number.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The way it is set up depends on the first characters of the project number. These characters serve as keys for coding projects."
claims.notes: The second sentence, which the lane omitted, is what actually supports the 'coding key' half of the claim.

claims.claim_text: A mask can be extended later but never shortened once projects exist on it — numbering is effectively immutable.
claims.evidence_quote: you cannot take anything away if WBSs have already been created using this project coding mask.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: "Even though you can make additions to the coding masks later, you cannot take anything away if WBSs have already been created using this project coding mask."
claims.notes: The claim's trailing gloss 'numbering is effectively immutable' overshoots the source, which explicitly permits later ADDITIONS. Use 'append-only once projects exist', not 'immutable'.

claims.claim_text: A coding key can be blocked so that no new projects may be created under it.
claims.evidence_quote: You cannot create new projects with this coding key if you maintain a blocking checkbox.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "you can maintain blocking checkboxes for standard structures (LkS) and operative structures (Lck). You cannot create new projects with this coding key if you maintain a blocking checkbox."
claims.notes: Two separate blocking flags exist (standard vs operative structures); the claim collapses them into one.

claims.claim_text: The coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are derived from the project ID.
claims.evidence_quote: The project coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are determined from the project ID.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The project coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are determined from the project ID."
claims.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. SOURCING CAVEAT: the page renders under 'Production Engineering and Operations for Complex Assembly', Version 2025 FPS01 (Feb 2026), and opens 'Follow the steps here to define a project coding mask for complex assembly projects.' The quoted sentence is itself stated unconditionally, so the claim holds, but this is a product-specific how-to page, not the general PS coding-mask documentation.

claims.claim_text: A WBS element ID including project ID and separators is capped at 24 characters.
claims.evidence_quote: The total length of a WBS ID, including project ID and all special characters, must not exceed 24 characters.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The total length of a WBS ID, including project ID and all special characters, must not exceed 24 characters." The page also states you can assign up to 5 characters for the project coding ID.
claims.notes: SOURCING CAVEAT (same page as R01-026): the ONLY source the lane offers for the 24-character cap is a Complex Assembly (PEO) how-to page. The sentence is unconditional so the verdict stands, but this is a load-bearing field-length constraint for the Zoho ID design and deserves a second, general PS citation before it is used as a hard design rule.

claims.claim_text: With a coding mask, the system derives hierarchy level from the WBS number; the shortest number becomes level 1.
claims.evidence_quote: The WBS element with the shortest number is created in level 1.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The WBS element with the shortest number is created in level 1."

claims.claim_text: The mask must contain enough separators to represent every intended hierarchy level.
claims.evidence_quote: enough dashes to model all the levels in the project hierarchy.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Appears in the Prerequisites section: "In this coding mask you entered enough dashes to model all the levels in the project hierarchy."
claims.notes: Source names dashes specifically; the claim generalises to 'separators'. Harmless but worth noting the mask separator in the example is a dash.

claims.claim_text: A configurable special character acts as input help that auto-prefixes the parent WBS number during entry.
claims.evidence_quote: the system copies the number of the higher-level WBS elements into the field.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "If you enter the special character in the WBS element field in your project, the system copies the number of the higher-level WBS elements into the field. If the new WBS element is the first one in the project hierarchy, the system copies the project definition." Worked example uses '@' and shows @-20 without a mask vs @20 with mask A-000-XXX-00-00, yielding A-123-LDZ-10-20.
claims.notes: The root-element fallback (copies the project definition) and the separator-suppression-under-mask behaviour are both material to a Zoho ID-entry UX and were not captured in the lane.

claims.claim_text: Operative indicators define what role a WBS element plays during project execution.
claims.evidence_quote: You use operative indicators to define the characteristics of a WBS element and to specify what tasks the WBS element will perform during project execution.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "You use operative indicators to define the characteristics of a WBS element and to specify what tasks the WBS element will perform during project execution."
claims.notes: Tier 2 only, as the lane's gap #1 correctly flags.

claims.claim_text: Planning element flags a WBS element as one on which costs may be planned.
claims.evidence_quote: WBS elements for which you want to plan costs are flagged as planning elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "WBS elements for which you want to plan costs are flagged as planning elements."
claims.notes: Tier-2 product-behaviour statement, accepted at that tier. No Tier-1 corroboration exists in this lane for the planning-element indicator specifically.

claims.claim_text: Account assignment element flags a WBS element as a valid target for actual cost postings.
claims.evidence_quote: WBS elements to which you want to post actual costs are flagged as account assignment elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "WBS elements to which you want to post actual costs are flagged as account assignment elements."
claims.notes: Partially corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-040.

claims.claim_text: Billing element flags a WBS element as one where revenue may be planned or posted.
claims.evidence_quote: WBS elements where you want to plan or post revenues are flagged as billing elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "WBS elements where you want to plan or post revenues are flagged as billing elements."
claims.notes: Corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-035.

claims.claim_text: A billing element is a structure element (project or WBS element) against which revenue can be planned and posted.
claims.evidence_quote: Billing Element is a project structure element against which a revenue can be planned and posted.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Billing Element is a project structure element against which a revenue can be planned and posted. It can either be a project or a WBS element."
claims.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition page, but the definition itself is generic and matches the Tier-2 classic-PS statement in R01-034, so no scope downgrade.

claims.claim_text: Billing elements cannot nest: none may sit inside another billing element's subtree.
claims.evidence_quote: However, a billing element cannot have another billing element in its subtree, nor can it be part of the subtree of another billing element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The quote matches verbatim, but it sits inside the 'Billing Element' page of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Enterprise Projects), under 'Characteristics of a Billing Element'. The companion page (WBS Maintenance) files the same rule under a heading literally titled 'Special Rules for Projects with Revenue'.
claims.notes: HIGHEST IMPACT SCOPE ERROR IN THE LANE. Narrower true statement: 'In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects, in projects with revenue, billing elements cannot nest.' Classic on-premise SAP PS - the variant Atha Group is migrating FROM - imposes no such non-nesting constraint on the billing-element indicator. Encoding a non-nesting validation in the Zoho model on this basis would reject legitimate legacy SAP PS hierarchies at migration.

claims.claim_text: Every WBS element beneath a billing element inherits the same functional area and profit center.
claims.evidence_quote: All the WBS elements in the subtree of a billing element must have the same functional area and profit center as the billing element. When you create, include, or indent a WBS element below a billing element, these values are adjusted automatically.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote matches verbatim but appears under the heading 'Special Rules for Projects with Revenue' on the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition WBS Maintenance page. The rule is conditional on the project being a revenue project in that variant.
claims.notes: Narrower true statement: applies to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects, in projects with revenue, below a billing element. Note also the second sentence the lane omitted: the values are FORCE-ADJUSTED automatically, not merely validated - a materially different behaviour to implement.

claims.claim_text: A revenue-bearing project must contain at least one billing element.
claims.evidence_quote: A project with revenue must contain at least one billing element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote matches verbatim. 'A project with revenue' is a named project-profile type in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (see the Project Profiles page), not a generic descriptor.
claims.notes: Narrower true statement: in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a project created with the 'Project with Revenue' profile must contain at least one billing element. The lane's claim_text reads as a universal accounting principle.

claims.claim_text: Settlement rules may not be entered on WBS elements inside a billing element subtree.
claims.evidence_quote: You can maintain settlement rule for WBS elements. However, you will not be able to enter any settlement rule on the WBS elements in the billing element subtree.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote matches, but the lane dropped the preceding sentence that establishes the general rule is the opposite: settlement rules CAN be maintained on WBS elements; the prohibition is the exception inside a billing-element subtree, in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.
claims.notes: Narrower true statement as given in replacement_quote. Scope: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects. Dropping the first sentence inverts the reader's default assumption about settlement rules.

claims.claim_text: A network can only be assigned to a WBS element that is flagged as an account assignment element.
claims.evidence_quote: To be able to assign a network to a WBS element, you must first identify the WBS element as an account assignment element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "To be able to assign a network to a WBS element, you must first identify the WBS element as an account assignment element."
claims.notes: Classic on-premise PS. Correctly scoped.

claims.claim_text: A profile checkbox can force the account assignment flag on for every WBS element in the project.
claims.evidence_quote: The All Acct Asst Elem checkbox sets the account assignment checkbox for all WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The All Acct Asst Elem checkbox sets the account assignment checkbox for all WBS elements."

claims.claim_text: A profile setting can restrict a project to a single top-level (root) WBS element.
claims.evidence_quote: Using the Only One Root checkbox, you define that there can only be one top WBS element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Using the Only One Root checkbox, you define that there can only be one top WBS element."
claims.notes: Implies multi-root WBS is possible by default in classic PS - a structural fact worth carrying into the Zoho model.

claims.claim_text: The statistical flag decides whether a WBS element can be debited with real costs or only statistically.
claims.evidence_quote: The Statistical checkbox determines whether costs can be debited from a WBS element or whether statistical costs can only be posted for it.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The Statistical checkbox determines whether costs can be debited from a WBS element or whether statistical costs can only be posted for it."
claims.notes: Tier-2 behaviour statement; corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-046.

claims.claim_text: Setting the statistical flag on a project propagates it to every WBS element in that project hierarchy.
claims.evidence_quote: A statistical project is used for planning and monitoring purposes. When you set the statistical flag for a project, this flag applies to the WBS elements present in the project hierarchy. Upon saving the project for the first time, you cannot change the selection of this flag.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote matches, but it describes the 'Statistical Project' PROJECT PROFILE TYPE in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The page adds a hard irreversibility rule the lane omitted entirely: after first save the flag cannot be changed. It also requires a default cost center at WBS level.
claims.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition statistical projects. The omitted irreversibility-after-first-save rule and the mandatory default cost center are both design-relevant and should be added.

claims.claim_text: Statistical WBS elements can neither be settled nor carry overhead.
claims.evidence_quote: Statistical WBS elements cannot be settled or carry overheads.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote matches verbatim on the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Profiles page.
claims.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The 'cannot be settled' half IS independently corroborated for classic PS by the source of R01-046 (which states the statistical designation prevents settlement); the 'cannot carry overheads' half has Cloud-only support in this lane.

claims.claim_text: The statistical indicator is set from the model order or project profile, or directly on the master record.
claims.evidence_quote: You define the order or WBS element as 'statistical' by setting an indicator in the model order or the project profile.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: "You define the order or WBS element as 'statistical' by setting an indicator in the model order or the project profile (or directly in the master record of the order or WBS element)." The page also states the statistical designation prevents settlement and limits use to planning and budget monitoring.
claims.notes: The lane's quote truncated before the parenthetical that supports the claim's third route ('directly on the master record'); the full sentence does support it.

claims.claim_text: Project type is a classification attribute usable as a selection criterion in reporting.
claims.evidence_quote: The Project Type can be used as a selection criterion in the Information System.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The Project Type can be used as a selection criterion in the Information System."

claims.claim_text: A Level of Detail setting controls how many hierarchy levels are expanded when a project is opened.
claims.evidence_quote: The Level of Detail field specifies the number of hierarchy levels that the system displays when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The Level of Detail field specifies the number of hierarchy levels that the system displays when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction."
claims.notes: First re-fetch returned a truncated form; second targeted exact-string pass confirmed the full sentence including 'when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction'.

claims.claim_text: Tabular overviews can label WBS elements by key, short ID or description, configurably.
claims.evidence_quote: The Display Options field determines whether WBS elements are mainly displayed according to key, short ID, or description in tabular overviews.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "The Display Options field determines whether WBS elements are mainly displayed according to key, short ID, or description in tabular overviews."
claims.notes: Absent from the first re-fetch extract; confirmed present verbatim on a second targeted exact-string pass.

claims.claim_text: A network represents the sequence of activities in a project (or of a single activity within it).
claims.evidence_quote: A network can represent the sequence of activities in a project or the sequence of a single activity within a project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "A network can represent the sequence of activities in a project or the sequence of a single activity within a project."
claims.notes: Verified twice: WebFetch and in-app browser.

claims.claim_text: Networks are the basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates and resources.
claims.evidence_quote: Networks are used as a basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates, and resources.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "During the life of a project, networks are used as a basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates, and resources.(such as personnel, machines, PRTs, materials, documents, and drawings)."
claims.notes: The lane's quote drops the leading 'During the life of a project,' but is otherwise an exact substring.

claims.claim_text: SAP PS networks are activity-on-node graphs, not activity-on-arrow.
claims.evidence_quote: In the Project System networks are activity-on-mode networks.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The page reads 'activity-on-MODE networks', not 'activity-on-node'. Verified twice independently: once via WebFetch and once by rendering the page in the in-app browser, which returned the same word. The page nowhere mentions 'activity-on-arrow' and draws no contrast with any alternative network notation.
claims.notes: TWO PROBLEMS. (1) The evidence_quote is not verbatim - the researcher silently corrected what is almost certainly a typo in the SAP source without flagging it, which breaks quote traceability. (2) The claim's second half, 'not activity-on-arrow', has no basis in the source at all; it is an inference. The substantive point may well be true, but this lane does not evidence it. Re-source from a page that names the precedence-diagramming method explicitly before relying on it.

claims.claim_text: The network header carries assignments to project definition, WBS element or sales document plus default values.
claims.evidence_quote: Assignments to other objects, for example, project definition, WBS element or sales document
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Assignments to other objects, for example, project definition, WBS element or sales document" - appears in the Network Headers section.

claims.claim_text: In header-assigned networks the header costing values are binding for the whole network rather than defaults.
claims.evidence_quote: In header-assigned networks the values in the Costing section of the supplementary data screen of the network header are not default values
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: "In header-assigned networks the values in the Costing section of the supplementary data screen of the network header are not default values, but are binding for the whole network."
claims.notes: The lane's quote stops before 'but are binding for the whole network' - the clause that actually carries the claim. Full sentence supports it.

claims.claim_text: Assigning a network header to a project definition allows the project dates to be copied into network basic dates.
claims.evidence_quote: you can copy the dates from the project definition into the basic dates of the network.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "you can copy the dates from the project definition into the basic dates of the network."

claims.claim_text: Assigning a network to a WBS element implies the project definition assignment automatically.
claims.evidence_quote: the project definition will be copied automatically when the assignment is made.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "the project definition will be copied automatically when the assignment is made."

claims.claim_text: An activity has a duration, a defined start and finish, is uninterrupted, consumes resources and incurs costs.
claims.evidence_quote: They have a defined start and a defined finish.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The page attributes the five characteristics to German standard DIN 69 900: "They have a duration. They have a defined start and a defined finish. They are processed without interruption. Resources are needed to execute them. They incur costs."
claims.notes: The lane's evidence_quote covers only one of the five characteristics the claim asserts; the other four are on the same page, so the claim holds. Worth recording that this is a DIN 69 900 definition SAP adopts, not an SAP-invented rule.

claims.claim_text: Activities are resource-consuming: resources are required to execute them.
claims.evidence_quote: Resources are needed to execute them.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Resources are needed to execute them."

claims.claim_text: Internally processed activities capture work by machines or persons and feed capacity requirement planning.
claims.evidence_quote: you determine the amount of Work produced by machines or persons, and use this information in resource planning to plan the capacity requirement.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "you determine the amount of Work produced by machines or persons, and use this information in resource planning to plan the capacity requirement."

claims.claim_text: Externally processed activities represent services bought from other companies and run through purchasing.
claims.evidence_quote: Using external processing you determine which services are required from other companies to carry out the project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Using external processing you determine which services are required from other companies to carry out the project."
claims.notes: The source sentence does not itself say 'run through purchasing'; that part of the claim_text is not carried by the quoted sentence.

claims.claim_text: Service activities plan planned and unplanned external services, procured through purchasing.
claims.evidence_quote: Using External Services Management you plan unplanned and planned services for carrying out the project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: "Using External Services Management you plan unplanned and planned services for carrying out the project."
claims.notes: As with R01-060, 'procured through purchasing' is not in the quoted sentence.

It omits (a) the MAX(plan, actual+commitment) rule for assigned networks/orders, (b) settlement debits, (c) settlement credits, (d) statistical actual costs. Implementing 'assigned = commitments + actuals' literally will UNDERSTATE assigned value and let projects overspend. The Budget Value Display page is a UI field glossary, not the calculation spec. claims.claim_text: Tolerance limits are keyed on a three-part combination of budget profile, transaction group and action, and may be expressed as relative or absolute variance.
claims.evidence_quote: You can define relative or absolute variance from budget values as tolerance limits for budget profile/transaction group/action combinations.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim: 'You can define relative or absolute variance from budget values as tolerance limits for budget profile/transaction group/action combinations.' BUT the page is FUNDS MANAGEMENT documentation — its action list reads 'Warning with Mail to funds center manager', and 'funds center' is Funds Management master data with no Project System equivalent.
claims.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: in SAP Funds Management, tolerance limits are keyed on budget profile / transaction group / action and may be relative or absolute. The record presents this as generic SAP tolerance grammar feeding a Project System budget design without any module caveat. R03.json's own gaps list admits the PS-specific 'Define Tolerance Limits' IMG page was never reached. PS does have its own Define Tolerance Limits activity (IMG path confirmed on the assigned-values page at R03-012), so the grammar is plausibly shared — but that is unproven from this source.

claims.claim_text: If no tolerance limit is found for a posting, SAP permits the posting - the control is opt-in and fails open, not closed.
claims.evidence_quote: If no tolerance limit is found, the posting is permitted.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim: 'If no tolerance limit is found, the posting is permitted.' Same Funds Management page as R03-038.
claims.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: in Funds Management availability control, a posting for which no tolerance limit is found is permitted. HIGH-STAKES OVERSTATEMENT: the record generalises this into 'the control is opt-in and fails open, not closed' as a design principle for the whole budget-availability build. Fail-open is a control-design decision that must not rest on a cross-module inference. It IS indirectly corroborated for PS by R03-012 (undefined ++ transaction group causes costs to be excluded from assigned value), which points the same way — but that is corroboration, not proof. Confirm against the PS 'Define Tolerance Limits' IMG page before relying on fail-open.

claims.claim_text: Action 1 is a pure warning: the user is told the tolerance limit is exceeded but the posting is not rejected.

claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim: 'The system informs you that the tolerance limit is being exceeded. However, the posting in question is not rejected.' Page title 'Availability Control Actions'; module confirmed as Funds Management.

The SUBSTANCE is independently corroborated Tier-1 and PS-side by R03-087 (warning-type limit still allows budget use), so the behaviour is safe to design against; the 'action 1/2/3' numbering is not proven to be PS terminology from this source.

claims.claim_text: Action 3 is a hard stop: a posting that breaches the action-3 tolerance limit is rejected and an error message is generated.

claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim: 'If a posting leads to the action 3 tolerance limit being exceeded, the system rejects the posting and generates an error message.' Funds Management page.
claims.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: Funds Management action 3 rejects the posting with an error. Substance corroborated PS-side by R03-088 (error-type limit blocks purchase orders/requisitions). Same module-scope caveat as R03-040.

claims.notes: THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING RECORD IN THE LANE AND IT REMAINS UNSOURCED. The verifier independently re-ran the search and additionally captured the S/4HANA Cloud 'Budget Availability Control' root page (30cb8dea...) that R03.json could not capture; it says only 'the budget availability control calculates the available budget' and prints no formula. R03's negative result therefore STANDS and is now double-confirmed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD: (1) the closest first-party wording is on a DIFFERENT page than the one cited — see replacement_quote from fd3dde531ed3424de10000000a174cb4, which names 'available project budget' and 'available released budget' as the quantities tested for sufficiency; cite that instead. ( = Plan costs of the networks or activities) = Plan total'
claims.notes: CONFIRMED with explicit '+' operators and a terminating '= Plan total'. NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH ASSIGNED VALUE: SAP prints the arithmetic for Plan total but NOT for assigned value or available budget. That asymmetry is itself evidence that the available-budget formula at R03-113 is genuinely absent from the documentation rather than merely unfound.

claims.claim_text: A commitment identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials or services already requested or ordered.
claims.evidence_quote: Identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials and services that you have requested or ordered.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Definition section opens verbatim: 'Identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials and services that you have requested or ordered.'
claims.notes: Page title 'Commitments', PS 2025 FPS01.

claims.claim_text: Commitments reserve funds for costs that will be incurred at a future date.
claims.evidence_quote: Commitments reserve funds for costs that will be incurred at a future date.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Second sentence of the Definition, verbatim.

claims.claim_text: SAP distinguishes three commitment types by account assignment object: order commitment, cost center commitment, and project commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: Commitments Management distinguishes between three types of commitments, depending on the account assignment object:
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, followed by the enumerated Order / Cost Center / Project Commitment list. Independently corroborated on learning.sap.com ('Commitments management distinguishes three types of commitments, depending on the account assignment object').

claims.claim_text: A project commitment is initially assigned to a project or to a work breakdown structure element.
claims.evidence_quote: The commitment is initially assigned to a project, or to a work breakdown structure element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under 'Project Commitment'.

claims.claim_text: Purchase requisitions express an internal requirement and are freely changeable; purchase orders are contractual and cannot be changed unilaterally.
claims.evidence_quote: Purchase orders are contractual requests to a vendor, to supply certain goods or services according to the agreed conditions.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Both halves of the claim are carried by the page. PR half: 'Purchase requisitions define the internal requirement for a material or a service. Purchase requisitions have a control function and you can change them at any time.' PO half: the quoted sentence plus 'No short-term, unilateral changes can be made.'
claims.notes: The evidence_quote alone only carries the PO half; the PR half is carried by adjacent text on the same page.

claims.claim_text: Funds commitments reserve funds for costs that are fairly certain but not yet tied to a requisition or order.
claims.evidence_quote: You can use Funds Commitments to reserve funds for costs you are fairly certain to incur
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'You can use Funds Commitments to reserve funds for costs you are fairly certain to incur, but you cannot yet assign to a specific business transaction (such as, a purchase order or a purchase requisition).'

claims.claim_text: Purchase requisition commitment equals the remaining requisition quantity multiplied by the requisition price.
claims.evidence_quote: The system calculates purchase requisition commitments from the remaining quantity of a purchase requisition, which it multiplies with the price
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence ends '...which it multiplies with the price from the purchase requisition' - the price basis is explicitly the REQUISITION price.
claims.notes: Deliverable is Internal Orders (CO-OM-OPA) 6.0 EHP2, flagged 'Out of Maintenance'. Mechanism is unchanged in the S/4HANA PS topics but the citation is to a legacy ERP deliverable.

claims.claim_text: PR commitments are reduced on a quantity basis by purchase orders that reference the corresponding purchase requisition.
claims.evidence_quote: The system reduces PReq commitments on a quantity basis, using purchase orders referring to the corresponding purchase requisition.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, first sentence of Features.
claims.notes: Load-bearing for anti-double-count: PR relief is driven by the referencing PO, on QUANTITY.

claims.claim_text: A PR commitment goes to zero either via a purchase order for the full amount or via a change to the requisition.
claims.evidence_quote: The system reduces a PReq commitment to zero using a purchase order with the full amount, or using a change in the purchase requisition.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim.

claims.claim_text: Worked example: a requisition of 5 pieces at EUR 1500.00 creates a purchase requisition commitment of EUR 7500.00.
claims.evidence_quote: You create a purchase requisition for 5 PCs at EUR 1500.00. This leads to a purchase requisition commitment of EUR 7500.00.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. 5 x 1500 = 7500 checks out.

claims.claim_text: Ordering only part of a requisition reduces the PR commitment proportionally at the requisition price, not the PO price.
claims.evidence_quote: The system reduces the purchase requisition commitment in proportion to quantity to EUR 3,000.00 (3 x EUR 1,500.00 = EUR 4,500.00).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote is verbatim INCLUDING its confusing arithmetic. Full worked example: PR 5 PC @ EUR 1500 = 7500 commitment. PO for 3 PC @ EUR 2000 creates a PO commitment of 6000. 'The system reduces the purchase requisition commitment in proportion to quantity to EUR 3,000.00 (3 x EUR 1,500.00 = EUR 4,500.00).' Correct reading: the PR commitment is relieved BY 4,500 (3 units x the REQUISITION price 1,500), leaving a residual balance of 3,000 (2 units x 1,500). The parenthetical is the reduction amount, not the resulting balance.
claims.notes: LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO MIS-READ. The claim ('at the requisition price, not the PO price') is exactly right and is the whole point of the example - the PO price of 2,000 never touches the PR relief. But the SAP sentence reads as self-contradictory on its face, so any downstream implementer who copies it verbatim without this gloss will get the residual wrong. Corroborated by the S/4HANA Cloud PSM lesson: 'the open amount is calculated by considering the open quantity first. This mechanism avoids open amounts in the case of price decreases.'

claims.claim_text: The purchase requisition commitment forms part of availability control against the project budget.
claims.evidence_quote: The resulting purchase requisition commitment also forms part of the availability control.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, final sentence of the topic.

claims.claim_text: Purchase order commitments reduce the referenced purchase requisition commitment; PO commitments are then reduced by goods/invoice receipt logic.
claims.evidence_quote: Purchase order commitments reduce each purchase requisition commitment by referencing to a purchase requisition.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim in Process flow.
claims.notes: This is the PR->PO leg of the anti-double-count chain.

claims.claim_text: Purchase order commitments are reduced according to the goods receipt / invoice receipt logic.
claims.evidence_quote: Purchase order commitments are reduced according to the goods / invoice receipt logic .
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim including the stray space before the period.
claims.notes: Note this sentence states the GR/IR logic exists but does NOT itself say which of GR or IR fires; it forward-references 'Reducing Purchase Order Commitments to Zero'. Do not cite this record alone as the GR-vs-IR rule.

claims.claim_text: Commitments Management must be explicitly activated before commitment values are recorded.
claims.evidence_quote: You must activate Commitments Management before you can use it.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Prerequisites.

claims.claim_text: The purchase order commitment is the order value for which no actual costs have yet been incurred.
claims.evidence_quote: It is the value of goods ordered, but for which no actual costs have yet been incurred.
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'The system derives purchase order commitments from the order value. It is the value of goods ordered, but for which no actual costs have yet been incurred.'

claims.claim_text: A purchase order only produces a commitment if it is account-assigned to an order, cost center, or project.
claims.evidence_quote: For this data transfer to take place from Purchasing, the purchase order must be assigned to an order, a cost center, or a project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Prerequisites.

claims.claim_text: Commitments are dated by the expected delivery date, not the purchase order creation date.
claims.evidence_quote: You create commitments using the expected delivery date, not the date the purchase order was created.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim.
claims.notes: Period-allocation rule: commitment is dated by expected delivery date. Corroborated by COOI field BUDAT = 'expected debit date (delivery date)' on the spmm wiki.

claims.claim_text: The purchase order commitment includes anticipated delivery costs, managed separately from the order value itself.
claims.evidence_quote: A purchase order commitment includes anticipated delivery costs. These costs are managed separately by the system.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Delivery Costs.
claims.notes: SCOPE CAVEAT the blueprint must carry: this is CLASSIC commitment management. The S/4HANA NEW commitment management lesson lists as an explicit restriction 'No separate commitments for freight costs are possible.' Do not assume separate freight commitments under the new ACDOCA-extension-ledger solution.

claims.claim_text: Delivery costs within a commitment are displayed individually by origin such as freight, duty, and packaging.
claims.evidence_quote: They are displayed individually according to origin (for example, freight costs, duty costs, packaging).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Corroborated on the spmm wiki: 'The delivery costs are displayed individually according to origin (for example, freight costs, duty costs, packaging) on CO side.'

claims.claim_text: A purchase order item can be split across several account assignment objects; the commitment is updated on each accordingly.
claims.evidence_quote: The system updates the purchase order commitment on the corresponding account assignment objects accordingly.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Multiple Account Assignment, preceded by 'you can assign a purchase order item to several account assignment objects'.

claims.claim_text: Re-assigning a purchase order item to a different cost object is allowed only while no actual costs have been incurred.
claims.evidence_quote: You can only do this if no actual costs have yet been incurred. Therefore, no goods receipt or invoice receipt may already have occurred.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Reassignment. Independently corroborated on the spmm wiki: 'The account information on the purchasing order can only be changed if no goods receipt or invoices have been posted.'
claims.notes: Two independent sources agree. Safe to treat as a hard rule.

claims.claim_text: The system reduces purchase order commitments to zero according to goods or invoice receipts and converts them into actual costs.
claims.evidence_quote: The system reduces purchase order commitments to zero according to goods or invoice receipts and converts them into actual costs.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, opening sentence of Use on 'Reducing Purchase Order Commitments to Zero', PS 2025 FPS01.
claims.notes: CORE anti-double-count statement. The commitment is not merely cancelled, it is CONVERTED into actual cost - which is exactly why the Assigned column (actual + commitment) stays flat across the conversion.

claims.claim_text: The goods receipt indicator on the purchase order item decides whether commitment reduction and actual cost arise at GR or at IR.
claims.evidence_quote: The goods receipt indicator in the purchase order determines when the commitment is reduced and actual costs are set up
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim: 'The goods receipt indicator in the purchase order determines when the commitment is reduced and actual costs are set up (that is, in the detail screen for the purchase order item).'
claims.notes: CONFIRMED AS QUOTED BUT INCOMPLETE AS A DESIGN RULE - see contradictions[0]. The GR indicator is only the FIRST of two gates. The 'goods receipt non-valuated' flag (EKPO/EKBP-WEUNB) is the second, and it can send relief to the invoice even when the GR indicator IS set. Any anti-double-count implementation keying solely on the GR indicator will mis-time relief on non-valuated-GR purchase orders.

claims.claim_text: With the GR indicator set on the purchase order item, the commitment is reduced when goods are received.
claims.evidence_quote: GR indicator set: Commitment is reduced when goods are received.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim: 'GR indicator set: Commitment is reduced when goods are received.'
claims.notes: Same two-gate caveat as R04-024: true when the GR is VALUATED. Where GR is non-valuated the invoice reduces instead.

claims.claim_text: Reduction to zero is quantity-driven, so quantity-based commitment management is required; value-based management is an alternative configuration.
claims.evidence_quote: As the quantity (down to zero) determines the reduction of a purchase order commitment to zero, you need quantity-based commitment management.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, plus the alternative: 'If values for purchase orders, goods to be delivered, and invoices are to determine the reduction (to zero) of a purchase order commitment, then you need value-based commitment management. To set up value-based commitment management per unit of measurement, choose General Settings > Check Unit of Measurement in Customizing.'
claims.notes: Both halves of the claim carried. Configuration point is the unit of measure (T006-KZWOB / transaction CUNI per the spmm wiki), i.e. quantity-vs-value is a per-UoM setting, not a global switch.

claims.claim_text: Purchase orders for services are monitored on the basis of value, not quantity, unlike material purchase orders.
claims.evidence_quote: Unlike purchase orders for materials, those for services are monitored on the basis of value, not quantity.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, in a Note block.
claims.notes: Services are the value-based exception on the PO side. Mirrored on the PR side by R04-040.

claims.claim_text: Entering a goods receipt or invoice receipt against a purchase order reduces the commitment proportionally.
claims.evidence_quote: You can reduce the purchase order commitment proportionally . To do this, you need to enter a goods receipt or invoice receipt
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim including the stray space: 'You can reduce the purchase order commitment proportionally . To do this, you need to enter a goods receipt or invoice receipt for a purchase order.'
claims.notes: Note the disjunction 'or' - the page does not say both fire. Which one fires is governed by R04-024/025/121 plus the valuation flag.

claims.claim_text: When the ordered quantity is under-delivered and no further delivery is expected, the Delivery completed indicator must be set at goods receipt.
claims.evidence_quote: In this case, you must set the "Delivery completed" indicator when you post the goods receipt.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, preceded by 'It could be that the total quantity for a purchase order item has not been delivered, but you expect no further deliveries.'
claims.notes: Corroborated twice: ELIKZ on the spmm wiki, and the PSM lesson ('In the event of partial delivery, you need to set the Delivery Complete indicator if the complete commitment is to be reduced').

claims.claim_text: At invoice entry a final-invoice indicator can be set on the purchase order item to signal no further invoices are expected.
claims.evidence_quote: you can set the indicator in the purchase order item to indicate that you do not expect any more incoming invoices
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'when you post the invoice, you can set the indicator in the purchase order item to indicate that you do not expect any more incoming invoices'.
claims.notes: This Tier-1 page never NAMES the indicator 'final invoice'. The name and field (EREKZ) come from the Tier-2 spmm wiki (R04-044) and the PSM lesson ('the Final Invoice indicator needs to be selected'). The behaviour is Tier-1; the field name is Tier-2.

claims.claim_text: Locking a purchase order item to prevent goods receipt is a documented way to reduce its commitment completely.
claims.evidence_quote: If you lock a purchase order item to prevent goods receipt for that item.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The quote matches, but the claim silently drops the very next sentence on the page, which is a hard precondition: 'If you lock a purchase order item to prevent goods receipt for that item. / This is possible providing no goods or invoices have been received.'
claims.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: locking a PO item reduces its commitment completely ONLY where no goods receipt and no invoice have yet been posted against that item. As written the claim reads as an unconditional cancellation lever and would license a 'lock => zero commitment' rule that is wrong for partially received or partially invoiced items. Downgraded.

claims.claim_text: Only completed purchase order items can be deleted; outstanding items require the Delivery completed indicator first.
claims.evidence_quote: If you wish to delete outstanding items, you need to set the "Delivery completed" indicator in the purchase order item first.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Both halves carried: 'You can only delete completed purchase order items (for example, there can be no deliveries or invoices outstanding...). If you wish to delete outstanding items, you need to set the "Delivery completed" indicator in the purchase order item first.' The page also notes deletion is a two-stage act: 'The purchase order item is marked for deletion but initially stays inactive in the system'.

claims.claim_text: In SAP's worked example an invoice priced above the PO raises both actual and assigned totals from 4650.00 to 6150.00.
claims.evidence_quote: 3. Invoice receipt for three PCs, USD 2,000.00 each
claims.narrower_true_statement: The quoted row label exists, but the claim misreads the table. The full table on 'Example: Reducing the Purchase Order Commitment' is: (1) PO 3 PC @ USD 1500 + USD 150 freight -> Actual ./. , Commitment 4650.00, Assigned 4650.00. (2) GR for two PC -> Actual 3100.00, Commitment 1550.00, Assigned 4650.00. (3) IR for three PC @ USD 2000 each -> Actual 4100.00, Commitment 2050.00, Assigned 6150.00. (4) GR for one PC -> Actual 6150.00, Commitment ./. , Assigned 6150.00. At the invoice-receipt step ACTUAL moves 3,100.00 -> 4,100.00, NOT 4,650.00 -> 6,150.00. Only ASSIGNED moves 4,650.00 -> 6,150.00 at that step. Actual only reaches 6,150.00 at step 4, the final goods receipt.
claims.notes: DOWNGRADED. NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: an invoice priced above the PO (2,000 vs 1,500) raises the ASSIGNED total from 4,650.00 to 6,150.00; the Actual column reads 4,100.00 at that step. Do not seed test scenarios from this claim as written - the numbers will not reconcile. Two further design-relevant facts visible in the table and not captured by any record in this lane: (a) the invoice for three PC is posted while only two PC had been received, and it INCREASES commitment from 1,550.00 to 2,050.00 rather than reducing it - a price/quantity revaluation, not a relief; (b) Assigned is flat across pure conversion steps (4,650.00 at steps 1 and 2) and only moves on genuine variance, which is precisely the anti-double-count invariant worth testing.

claims.claim_text: The final goods receipt reduces the purchase order commitment fully and converts it into actual costs.
claims.evidence_quote: You post the last goods receipt using a PC. The purchase order commitment is reduced and converted completely into actual costs.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, the topic's opening sentence.
claims.notes: Consistent with row 4 of the table (Commitment ./. , Actual 6150.00).

claims.claim_text: SAP commitment reports present three columns: Actual, Commitments, and Assigned defined as actual plus commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: Assigned (actual + commitment)
claims.narrower_true_statement: Column header of the report table reads exactly 'Assigned (actual + commitment)', alongside columns 'Actual' and 'Commitments'. The identical three-column header appears on the PS example page 337cd..., so this is corroborated across two deliverables (Controlling and Project System).
claims.notes: This is the definitional anchor for the whole anti-double-count design: Assigned = Actual + Commitment, so relief must debit one and credit the other to keep Assigned flat.

claims.claim_text: Freight added to a purchase order is included in the commitment: 3 pieces at 1500.00 plus 150.00 freight commits 4650.00.
claims.evidence_quote: 1. Purchase Order Three Pcs à USD 1500.00 + USD 150.00 Freight
claims.narrower_true_statement: Table row matches verbatim, and the prose states the total explicitly: 'the system creates a purchase order commitment of USD 4,650.00 for the order' and 'The order report displays the commitment of USD 4,650.00 resulting from the purchase order.' Arithmetic checks: 3 x 1500 + 150 = 4650.
claims.notes: Freight is inside the committed amount. Same classic-vs-new caveat as R04-019.

claims.claim_text: PO commitment reduction is driven by follow-on documents posted against the purchasing document, including goods receipt, invoice and credit memo.
claims.evidence_quote: the commitment reduction, and as consequence, the consumption confirmation, is processed based on the related documents posted against the purchasing document
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'For Purchasing orders, the commitment reduction, and as consequence, the consumption confirmation, is processed based on the related documents posted against the purchasing document like goods receipt (GR), invoices (IV), credit memo (CM), etc.'
claims.notes: Tier 2 (SAP-hosted support wiki, 'Additional Content'), behavioural claim, so CONFIRMED is permitted. Mechanism detail: relief is computed from the PO history table EKBE, debit documents SHKZG='S', credit documents SHKZG='H'.

claims.claim_text: The goods-receipt-non-valuated flag controls whether the commitment decreases at goods receipt or only when an invoice is posted.
claims.evidence_quote: controls whether the commitment is decreased when goods are received or when an invoice has been posted
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full passage: 'If in PO, the goods receipt flag is set, it means that incoming goods are expected. The flag \'goods unvalued\' available on the PO document, controls whether the commitment is decreased when goods are received or when an invoice has been posted. When the indicator "goods receipt non-valuated" is set, it means that the information from IV will be used to reduce the commitments created for the PO.' Section 6 names the field: EKBP-WEUNB. GR fields (WEMNG/WEWTW/WEWHW) drive relief when GR is valuated; invoice fields (REMNG/REWTW/REWHW) drive relief when GR is non-valuated.
claims.notes: THE DECISIVE RECORD FOR THE TASK. This is the only source in the lane that states the two-gate mechanism explicitly and names the controlling field. It is Tier 2. See contradictions[0] - the blueprint should not rest the GR-vs-IR switch on the Tier-1 GR-indicator sentence alone.

claims.claim_text: For quantity-based commitment items the reduction uses the goods receipt or invoice quantity, not its value.
claims.evidence_quote: For positions that are using quantity-based commitments, the commitments will be reduced based on the quantity from the goods receipt/invoice and not in the value.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim in section 3. Also: 'For purchasing orders, the commitments can be value based or quantity base handled, based on the unit of measure used on the PO' - checked via CUNI / T006-KZWOB.
claims.notes: Quantity-vs-value is decided per unit of measure, not per document. Corroborated Tier-1 by R04-026.

claims.claim_text: For non-service items purchase requisition commitment reduction is always quantity-based; value-based reduction applies only to service items.
claims.evidence_quote: For non-service items, the purchasing requisitions commitments reductions is always quantity based (note 355793).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Appears twice on the page (sections 3 and 5), verbatim, citing SAP Note 355793. Complementary sentence: 'For purchasing requisitions, the commitments reduction can only be valued based for service items.'
claims.notes: Corroborated by the PSM lesson: 'In PSM, budget management purchase requisitions are always reduced by quantity.' Underlying SAP Note 355793 was NOT independently retrieved - the note number is reported by the wiki, not verified.

claims.claim_text: Goods receipt cancellations and credit memos reverse consumption, reducing the recorded receipt values and quantities and restoring commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: Documents, that reduces the consumption, as goods receipt canceling or credit memo are used to reduce the values and quantities
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'Documents, that reduces the consumption, as goods receipt canceling or credit memo are used to reduce the values and quantities from the corresponding fields on EKBP. On EKBE credit documents are stored with SHKZG (Debit/credit indicator) = \'H\'.'
claims.notes: MINOR INFERENCE FLAGGED: the source says these documents reduce the CONSUMPTION values/quantities on EKBP. The claim's phrase 'restoring commitment' is the arithmetic consequence (open = purchased - reduced, per COOI WHGBTR in R04-046), not a sentence on the page. Sound, but it is a derivation.

claims.claim_text: Delivery costs are incorporated into the item effective price and are therefore also committed, then reduced by GR and invoice documents.
claims.evidence_quote: The reductions of the committed delivery cost are also processed for debit documents as GR and IV.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Both halves carried in section 7: 'The delivery costs are incorporated to the item effective price and for this reason, these values are also committed, once it also indicates consumption. The reductions of the committed delivery cost are also processed for debit documents as GR and IV.' Cites SAP Note 670489.
claims.notes: Delivery-cost history is a SEPARATE table (EKBZ, not EKBE) and is matched by condition step number STUNR. Relevant if the target model needs to relieve landed cost independently of goods value.

claims.claim_text: Setting the final delivery flag ELIKZ on the order item drives the commitment completely to zero on the delivery route.
claims.evidence_quote: the flag 'final delivery' (ELIKZ) is set in the order item, then the commitment will be completely reduced (set to zero)
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'If the commitment reduction takes place with goods delivery and the flag \'final delivery\' (ELIKZ) is set in the order item, then the commitment will be completely reduced (set to zero).'
claims.notes: Note the conditional opening the source states and the claim omits: 'If the commitment reduction takes place WITH GOODS DELIVERY'. The claim's own wording ('on the delivery route') preserves this, so no downgrade. Behaviour is corroborated Tier-1 by R04-029.

claims.claim_text: The same total-reduction behaviour applies on the invoice route when the final invoice flag EREKZ is set.
claims.evidence_quote: The same applies with commitment reduction via invoice with the flag 'final invoice' set (EREKZ).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Corroborated Tier-1 in behaviour (unnamed indicator) by R04-030 and by the PSM lesson's 'Final Invoice indicator'.
claims.notes: ELIKZ and EREKZ are the two independent 'force to zero' levers, one per route. A design that models only one of them will strand residual commitment on the other route.

claims.claim_text: Deleting a purchase order item also deletes the corresponding commitments.
claims.evidence_quote: When a position has been deleted (LOEKZ), the corresponding commitments are also deleted.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim.
claims.notes: Reconcile with Tier-1 R04-032: deletion is only permitted once the item is complete, so LOEKZ-driven commitment deletion presupposes the delivery-completed step.

claims.claim_text: Commitment line items store both original and open figures; open value equals purchased value minus reduced value.
claims.evidence_quote: WHGBTR - open value in local currency (purchased value – reduced value)
claims.narrower_true_statement: COOI field list verbatim, including GESMNG (purchased quantity), MEGBTR (open quantity = purchased - reduced), ORGWTH (purchased value in local currency), WHGBTR (open value = purchased - reduced), BUDAT (expected debit date/delivery date), plus 'fields that begin with \'ORG\' (original), represents the committed values'.
claims.notes: Gives the exact persisted shape for an open-commitment table: keep original and reduced separately, derive open. Directly reusable as the Zoho-side data model.

claims.claim_text: With multiple account assignment, partial invoice amounts are distributed either progressively (fill-up) or proportionally per the partial invoice indicator.
claims.evidence_quote: If you enter a partial invoice at invoice receipt, the system calculates the distribution of the costs in invoice verification
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim. Governing field named as EKPO-TWRKZ (Partial invoice indicator), with the two modes listed as 'On a progressive fill-up basis (Following Row)' and 'On a proportional basis', plus a worked 100-piece / 3-cost-centre table showing 350/280/70 proportional versus 500/200/0 progressive for a $700 partial invoice.
claims.notes: The worked distribution table is directly reusable as a test fixture for multi-account partial invoicing.

claims.claim_text: Purchase order account assignment can only be changed while no goods receipt or invoice has been posted.
claims.evidence_quote: The account information on the purchasing order can only be changed if no goods receipt or invoices have been posted.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim in section 8.
claims.notes: Duplicate of Tier-1 R04-022 from an independent source. Strong.

claims.claim_text: Invoices may carry account assignments not present on the purchase order; these unplanned values are distributed across the planned accounts.
claims.evidence_quote: Values from unplanned accounts are distributed among the planned accounts in “Follow in a row” way.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim (curly quotes preserved). Context: 'On invoices documents it\'s possible to change the account provided... In this case, this information will be treated as "UNPLANNED" (EKBE-XUNPL).'

claims.claim_text: SAP provides a repair report that rebuilds commitment data from the purchase order and its document history.
claims.evidence_quote: This report rebuilds the commitment information based on the purchasing order information and purchasing order history.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, describing report RKANBU01, cross-referenced to SAP Note 534993.
claims.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT found on a different page and not captured by this lane: the S/4HANA new-commitment-management lesson states 'The correction report RKANBU01, which is used to correct classic commitment (table COOI) can not be used to correct new commitment (table ACDOCA)! There\'s no report which automatically adjusts or corrects new commitment in ACDOCA.' A reconciliation/repair story modelled on RKANBU01 has no equivalent under the new solution.

claims.claim_text: Commitments for stock transport orders are switched on via a dedicated enhancement, i.e. they are not on by default.
claims.evidence_quote: ME_COMM_STO_ACTIVE_CHECK – commitments for stock transport orders.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The BAdI name matches verbatim, in a list introduced as: 'From 47.0 release, there are some BADI available that activate some functionalities: MEPOBADI_CHOICE_OBLIGO - commitments for release strategy /parked PO. ME_COMM_STO_ACTIVE_CHECK - commitments for stock transport orders. AC_DOCUMENT_PARKING_NO_UPDATE - commitments for parked invoices/credit memo'. The page nowhere states the DEFAULT state of STO commitments.
claims.notes: NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: SAP exposes BAdI ME_COMM_STO_ACTIVE_CHECK in connection with commitments for stock transport orders. The claim's second clause ('i.e. they are not on by default') is a reasonable but unstated inference from the word 'activate'. Low design impact, but flagged so the blueprint does not cite a default it cannot source. Consistent with the lane's own gap note that STO commitment behaviour was only reached indirectly.

claims.claim_text: A network-generated purchase requisition creates a PR commitment on the activity or WBS element account assignment object.
claims.evidence_quote: The purchase requisition results in purchase requisition commitments for the account assignment object (activity or WBS element).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Preceding sentence establishes the trigger: 'The network generates purchase requisitions for external processing activities, service activities, and material components procured externally (non-stock).'
claims.notes: learning.sap.com counts as Tier 1 for product behaviour under the gate; CONFIRMED holds under either tiering.

claims.claim_text: Converting the requisition to a purchase order produces a purchase order commitment carrying a different value type from the PR commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: When you convert the purchase requisition to a purchase order, it results in purchase order commitments for the account assignment object
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: '...it results in purchase order commitments for the account assignment object (this value type is different from the purchase requisition commitments).' The parenthetical carries the claim's value-type half.
claims.notes: Confirms only that the value types DIFFER. No source in this lane prints the actual value-type codes for PR vs PO commitment - the lane's own gap note on this is correct and still stands. Do not hard-code value type numbers.

claims.claim_text: Whether actual costs post at goods receipt or invoice receipt depends on the account assignment category (valuated vs non-valuated GR).
claims.evidence_quote: Based on the account assignment category of the purchase order, actual costs are posted upon goods receipt or invoice receipt
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'Based on the account assignment category of the purchase order, actual costs are posted upon goods receipt or invoice receipt (valuated, non-valuated goods receipt).'
claims.notes: CRITICAL DISTINCTION the blueprint must preserve: this sentence is about WHERE ACTUAL COSTS POST, and it attributes the switch to the ACCOUNT ASSIGNMENT CATEGORY (which determines valuated vs non-valuated GR). The Tier-1 PS page R04-024 attributes the COMMITMENT REDUCTION switch to the GR INDICATOR. Two different fields, two different (though coupled) effects. The claim text correctly says 'actual costs'. See contradictions[0].

claims.claim_text: Account assignment category F is the standard for order account assignment and produces a valuated goods receipt.
claims.evidence_quote: For account assignment category F, the good receipt is valuated.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Both halves carried: 'In the SAP standard system, you use account assignment category F for the account assignment of orders, which includes network headers, network activities, maintenance orders, internal orders, and manufacturing orders' and 'For account assignment category F, the good receipt is valuated.' (sic, 'good receipt').
claims.notes: Category F => valuated GR => GR is the relief and actual-cost event. Contrast category Q for project stock (R04-096).

claims.claim_text: Goods receipt for services is a two-step act: entering the services performed and then accepting them.
claims.evidence_quote: Goods receipt for services involves two steps: entering the services performed and accepting the services.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim.
claims.notes: Corroborated Tier-1 by the MM services process page (entry then acceptance as steps 8 and 9).

claims.claim_text: A service activity can hold a hierarchy of planned services plus value limits covering unplanned services.
claims.evidence_quote: it can also contain a hierarchy of planned services to be purchased and value limits for unplanned services
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, referring to a service activity.
claims.notes: The value limit for unplanned services is the nearest documented analogue to a construction variation allowance - consistent with the lane's gap note on contract variations.

claims.claim_text: Differences between the preliminary goods receipt value at net PO price and the invoice value post to the account assignment object.
claims.evidence_quote: You post any differences between the preliminary goods receipt value (net purchase order price) and invoice value to the account assignment object.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under External Processing: Goods Receipt, plus 'Price differences between the goods receipt and invoice receipt are also updated to the cost object.'
claims.notes: This is the variance leg that keeps GR-then-IR from either double-counting or under-counting: GR books at net PO price, IR books only the delta.

claims.claim_text: Non-stock component goods receipts post as expense to the activity, not to inventory accounts, at net purchase order price.
claims.evidence_quote: You post the goods receipt for the non-stock component as an expense, and not to inventory accounts.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, and the price basis is carried by the following sentences: 'The account assignment object is debited with the costs of externally procured materials. The costs are based on the net purchase order price.'

claims.claim_text: A price variance arising during invoice processing is posted to the activity that carried the goods receipt.
claims.evidence_quote: If a price variance occurs during invoice processing, the variance is posted to the activity.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Purchasing Process.

claims.claim_text: When commitment accounting is active for the controlling area, open purchase order items on a project are recorded as commitments.
claims.evidence_quote: If commitment accounting for the controlling area is active, the open purchase order items for the project are recorded as commitments.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Corroborated Tier-1 by R04-015 and by the spmm wiki's OKKP prerequisite (R04-117).
claims.notes: Also note from the new-commitment lesson: 'If Commitment Management is active in the controlling area, it is also automatically active for projects.'

claims.claim_text: The goods receipt reduces the project commitment by the amount of the purchase order value for the received quantity.
claims.evidence_quote: The goods receipt reduces the commitment by the amount of the purchase order value.
