claims.narrower_true_statement: Source sentence is exactly 'The goods receipt reduces the commitment by the amount of the purchase order value.' - with NO 'for the received quantity' qualifier.
claims.notes: The claim ADDS 'for the received quantity'. That addition makes the claim narrower and more accurate (it is required by Tier-1 R04-028 on proportional reduction and by the 337cd worked table, where a 2-of-3 GR relieves 3100 of 4650). Not an overstatement, but the qualifier is the verifier's/author's, not the source's. Do not attribute the qualifier to SAP.

claims.claim_text: Value type 11 records a posting as a statistical actual value, used for reporting project stock without real cost effect.
claims.evidence_quote: You use value type 11 to record a posting as a statistical actual value.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, in the context 'If the balance sheet inventory account is created as a cost element (category 90), you can report project stock statistically for all goods movements of the project stock using value type 11.'
claims.notes: Value type 11 = statistical actual. This is the one value-type code any source in this lane actually prints; the PR/PO commitment value types remain unsourced (see R04-053).

claims.claim_text: In S/4HANA the new commitment management stores commitments as forecast expenses in ACDOCA within an extension ledger.
claims.evidence_quote: In S/4HANA, commitments are forecast expenses that are saved in ACDOCA in the extension ledger.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Also: 'Creating an extension ledger for commitments activates the new commitment management based on posting documents in the journal' and 'the old commitment tables are still posted in parallel so that the old commitment reports and Budget Management continue to work.'
claims.notes: Both models run SIMULTANEOUSLY (COOI and ACDOCA). Any reconciliation design must decide which one is authoritative rather than assuming a single store.

claims.claim_text: Posting the actual goods receipt reverses the forecast purchasing cost in the commitment extension ledger, preventing double counting.
claims.evidence_quote: When the actual goods receipt for the purchase order is posted, the forecast material purchasing costs/the simulated postings are reversed in the enhancement ledger and the actual documents for the goods receipt/material costs are posted in the leading ledger. The value on the GR/IR account in the extension ledger is also reversed.
claims.narrower_true_statement: The recorded evidence_quote is NOT a contiguous string on the page: it silently elides '/the simulated postings' from the middle of the sentence. The claim itself is correct and the corrected full sentence is supplied as replacement_quote. A second, independent restatement of the same mechanism appears later on the page: 'When the goods receipt is saved, the forecast material purchasing costs are reversed in the extension ledger and posted as actual material costs in the leading ledger 0L. The amount on the GR/IR account is also reversed in the extension ledger.'
claims.notes: QUOTE DEFECT ONLY - substance stands. This is the S/4HANA-new-model expression of the anti-double-count invariant: the forecast is REVERSED in the extension ledger at the same moment the actual is posted in the leading ledger, so summing the two ledgers never double-counts. Replace the quote in the blueprint.

claims.claim_text: The new S/4HANA commitment management supports only WBS elements and cost centers as account assignment types.
claims.evidence_quote: Only projects (WBS elements) and cost centers are supported as account assignment types.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, first bullet of an explicitly 'complete list of all restrictions'. Other restrictions on the same list that bear directly on this engagement: 'No manual commitments are supported'; 'No commitment carry forward is supported'; 'Only purchase orders and purchase requisitions are supported'; 'No separate commitments for freight costs are possible'; 'Commitments from down payments are not supported'; 'A GR/IR account needs to be configured'; 'Purchase order or purchase requisition with account assignment G/L account of cost element category 90 is not supported... Therefore, an account assignment WBS element in combination with asset is not supported'; max 499 account assignments per PO (249 if referencing a PR).
claims.notes: HIGH VALUE, UNDER-CAPTURED BY THE LANE. Four of these restrictions directly contradict capabilities the lane records elsewhere for CLASSIC commitment management: freight commitments (R04-019/036), down-payment commitment interaction (R04-071), commitment carry-forward (R04-109/110/111), and the WBS-plus-asset assignment implied by the Investment Management down-payment records (R04-083..087). None of those contradictions are errors - they are classic-vs-new scope differences - but the blueprint MUST state which commitment model it is targeting or it will specify a system that cannot exist.

claims.claim_text: An order commitment arises in the amount of the order value and incoming goods reduce it.
claims.evidence_quote: An order commitment arises in the amount of the order value.
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'In this case, an order commitment arises in the amount of the order value.' The reduction half of the claim is carried separately: 'Business transactions such as incoming goods reduce commitments; Actual costs are incurred on the corresponding account assignment object. This happens until, for example, the "order" business transaction has been completed and the order commitment has been completely reduced.'
claims.notes: Both halves carried, from two adjacent sections. Also states the period placement: commitments are displayed 'for the cost element, fiscal year and period of the expected cost incidence' - consistent with Tier-1 R04-018 (delivery date, not PO date).

claims.claim_text: Only valuated goods receipts consume budget and reduce the purchase order commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: Only valuated goods receipts consume budgets and reduce the commitment from the purchase orders.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Goods Receipts, immediately followed by 'For non-valuated goods receipt, there is no financial impact.'
claims.notes: SCOPE: the lesson is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Public Sector Management budget management. Stated generally in the claim. Retained as CONFIRMED because the identical mechanism is independently sourced for general MM by the spmm wiki (EKBP-WEUNB, R04-038). Cite the pair, not this alone.

claims.claim_text: If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice is what reduces the commitment.
claims.evidence_quote: If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice reduces the commitment
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: 'If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice reduces the commitment of the purchase order. In this case, it is possible to change the proposed account assignments for the purchase order in the supplier invoice.' The PO-side summary on the same page states the whole rule in one line: 'Purchase orders and the correspondent budget consumption are reduced either by a valuated goods receipt or by supplier invoices if the goods receipt is non-valuated, or delivery is not expected.'
claims.notes: THE CLEANEST SINGLE STATEMENT OF THE ANSWER TO THE TASK QUESTION. Two branch conditions, not one: (a) GR non-valuated, or (b) no delivery expected (GR indicator not set). Triangulates exactly with Tier-1 R04-121 (branch b) and Tier-2 R04-038 (branch a). Same PSM scope caveat as R04-068.

claims.claim_text: After a valuated goods receipt the later invoice only moves the number if price or quantity changes are posted during invoice processing.
claims.evidence_quote: If the goods receipt was valuated, budget is only influenced if price/quantity changes are posted during invoice processing.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, plus 'The account assignments from the purchase orders cannot be changed in this case' and 'In case of price and quantity difference between the invoice and goods receipts, additional postings are generated using the GR/IR clearing program.'
claims.notes: This is the no-double-count guarantee on the valuated route: after a valuated GR the invoice is a VARIANCE-ONLY event. Independently demonstrated by the Tier-1 numeric table at 337cd..., where the over-priced invoice moves Assigned by exactly the variance. PSM scope caveat applies.

claims.claim_text: Down payments reduce the purchase order separately, using their own budget consumption amount type.
claims.evidence_quote: Down payments reduce the purchase orders separately (using a specific budget consumption amount type).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, plus the reversal rule the claim omits: 'This specific reduction is reversed whenever the down payment is cleared.'
claims.notes: The omitted second sentence matters for anti-double-counting: the down-payment reduction is TEMPORARY and unwinds on clearing, so a naive implementation that permanently relieves commitment on down payment will under-state commitment after clearing. The claim is PSM-scoped by its own vocabulary ('budget consumption amount type'), so no downgrade. Note the S/4HANA new commitment model does NOT support down-payment commitments at all (R04-066).

claims.claim_text: Purchase requisitions and their budget consumption are reduced by the purchase orders raised against them.
claims.evidence_quote: Purchase requisitions and the correspondent budget consumptions are reduced by purchase orders.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. The same page gives the quantity-first rule and a worked example that the lane did not capture: 'During commitment updating, purchase orders and purchase requisitions are reduced-quantity based. This means that the open amount is calculated by considering the open quantity first. This mechanism avoids open amounts in the case of price decreases... Purchase requisition: 10 x $10 = $100 (open commitment). Reduced by purchase order (lower price): 10 x $9 = $90 (open commitment). In this case, the purchase requisition is completely reduced because there are no quantities open to be ordered.'
claims.notes: HIGH VALUE ADDITION. This worked example closes the exact failure mode a value-based PR relief would create: ordering the FULL quantity at a LOWER price must still zero the PR commitment, leaving no $10 phantom residual. It is the price-decrease mirror of the Tier-1 price-increase example in R04-011. Recommend capturing as a first-class test scenario.

claims.claim_text: Unplanned delivery costs are not agreed in the purchase order and first appear when the invoice is received.
claims.evidence_quote: Unplanned delivery costs were not agreed on in the purchase order and are not entered until the invoice is received.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, opening sentence of Use. Deliverable 'Invoicing', 2025 FPS01.

claims.claim_text: Unplanned delivery costs are distributed automatically in the ratio of value invoiced so far to values in the current invoice.
claims.evidence_quote: The system distributes the unplanned delivery costs automatically in the ratio of the value invoiced so far to the values in the current invoice.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Applies to the 'Distributing Unplanned Delivery Costs to Invoice Items' option; a parallel variant distributes across goods items AND planned delivery cost items. BAdI MRM_UDC_DISTRIBUTE allows custom rules.
claims.notes: Distribution behaviour is one of three configurable options, not a single fixed rule.

claims.claim_text: Posting unplanned delivery costs to a separate G/L account means they do not debit stock accounts or account assignment objects.
claims.evidence_quote: The system posts unplanned delivery costs to a separate G/L account. Therefore, the unplanned delivery costs do not debit stock accounts or account assignment objects.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, under the heading 'Posting Unplanned Delivery Costs to a Separate G/L Account'. The page also adds: 'The system does not display unplanned delivery costs that were posted to a separate G/L account in the purchase order history.'
claims.notes: The claim correctly conditions on the separate-G/L-account option rather than generalising. Good scoping. The extra sentence about PO history invisibility is material for reconciliation design and is not captured by any record.

claims.claim_text: Unplanned distributed delivery costs cannot be distinguished from price variances in the purchase order history.
claims.evidence_quote: You cannot differentiate between unplanned distributed delivery costs and price variances in the purchase order history.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, in a Note titled 'Purchase order history'.
claims.notes: Known-limitation record; correctly flagged as such by the lane.

claims.claim_text: If the related goods items are already settled, unplanned delivery costs are entered as a subsequent debit on the settled invoice items.
claims.evidence_quote: you enter data for the unplanned delivery costs as a Subsequent Debit for the settled invoice items
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: 'If the goods items that the unplanned delivery costs refer to, have already been settled, you enter data for the unplanned delivery costs as a Subsequent Debit for the settled invoice items.'

claims.claim_text: Retention is the part of an invoice amount held back until a defined due date such as the end of a warranty period.
claims.evidence_quote: Part of an invoice amount that is retained until a defined due date (for example, the end of the warranty period)
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim Definition, continuing '...to ensure the delivery of materials or the performance of services as defined in the contract.'

claims.claim_text: Retention is defined on the purchase order as a percentage of purchase order value at header or item level and defaults into invoice verification.
claims.evidence_quote: In the purchase order, you define a retention as a percentage of the purchase order value at header or item level.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Defaulting half carried by 'The system transfers this data as default values to Logistics Invoice Verification (MM-IV-LIV)' and 'proposes the retention amount that it calculates in this way when you enter the invoice. You can overwrite all default values'. A third retention type exists that the claim does not mention - 'By guarantee of payment' - which is explicitly 'not relevant to the transfer of data to Logistics Invoice Verification'.

claims.claim_text: Planned delivery costs are excluded from the retention calculation base.
claims.evidence_quote: Plannend delivery costs are not included when retentions are calculated.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, including SAP's own typo 'Plannend'.
claims.notes: Quote fidelity is exact - the typo is SAP's, not the lane's.

claims.claim_text: Retention posts to financial accounting under a special G/L indicator, by default H.
claims.evidence_quote: The system transfers the special G/L indicator for retention (by default H, can also be defined manually) to financial accounting.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, plus 'you can define a different special G/L indicator for each company code'.
claims.notes: H is a default, configurable per company code - do not hard-code.

claims.claim_text: Retention cannot be combined with prepayment of an invoice.
claims.evidence_quote: You cannot use retention together with prepayment of an invoice.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, first bullet of constraints. A second constraint the lane did not capture: 'In case of multiple account assignment, no different tax codes are possible. If you use different tax codes, the system deletes the retention data and these fields are no longer ready for input.'
claims.notes: CONFIRMS THE LANE'S GAP NOTE: I re-read this entire page and it says NOTHING about retention affecting the purchase order commitment balance. The lane's 'treat as unknown' is correct and must not be quietly resolved downstream.

claims.claim_text: Down payments on investment measures are acquisition postings normally flagged by a separate cost element.
claims.evidence_quote: Down payments made for investment measures represent acquisition postings that are generally indicated by a separate cost element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, opening sentence of Use. Deliverable Investment Management (IM), 2025 FPS01.

claims.claim_text: Down payments can be assigned directly to an order or project, or to purchase orders that are themselves assigned to a project.
claims.evidence_quote: In addition to direct account assignment to an order or project, it is also possible to assign down payments to purchase orders.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, followed by 'These purchase orders can be assigned to an order or project.'

claims.claim_text: Down payments show only temporarily as costs on the project, posted through a primary cost element and cleared at settlement.
claims.evidence_quote: Posting as a primary cost element is necessary for the temporary display of down payments as costs in project/order cost accounting.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Settlement half carried by 'As a result of the periodic settlement to AuC, the down payments then increase the balance sheet during period-end closing and are posted to the corresponding reconciliation accounts of Asset Accounting.' Cost element category must be 1 (primary).
claims.notes: The word 'temporary' is SAP's own. Down payments inflate project cost only until settlement - a genuine double-count trap if the target system treats them as permanent actuals.

claims.claim_text: Down payment and its clearing must be settled together under the same settlement rule so they net to zero.
claims.evidence_quote: you must ensure that the down payment and down payment clearing are settled together with the same settlement rule
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, under Full Settlement, followed by 'This ensures that the down payment and down payment clearing also balance to zero for the settlement receivers.' A related caution: with foreign currencies, both must be posted with the same translation date or currency fluctuations break the netting.
claims.notes: The 'net to zero' phrasing in the claim is SAP's 'balance to zero'. Accurate.

claims.claim_text: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element and must be assigned directly to the WBS element.
claims.evidence_quote: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, followed by 'If you want to assign down payments to an investment measure, always assign them directly to the WBS element.'

claims.claim_text: Services actually performed are recorded on service entry sheets referencing the purchase order.
claims.evidence_quote: You enter services that have actually been performed by means of service entry sheets.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, step 8. Continues 'In doing so, you can reference the PO... Each individual service is recorded together with quantities and values.'
claims.notes: MM 6.0 EHP8 deliverable, in maintenance (not flagged out-of-maintenance).

claims.claim_text: Unplanned services entered against a purchase order value limit are recorded at precise value and checked against that limit.
claims.evidence_quote: The services are recorded with their precise value, and the system checks that the limit has not been exceeded.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, preceded by 'If a value limit for unplanned services has been set in the purchase order, you can maintain specifications for such services at the time you record their actual performance.'

claims.claim_text: Service acceptance can be separated from service entry to preserve the dual control principle.
claims.evidence_quote: You can separate the process of service acceptance from that of service entry in order to maintain the dual control principle.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, followed by 'However, it is also possible to have entry and acceptance carried out by the same individual or department' - i.e. separation is optional, not mandatory.
claims.notes: The claim says 'can be separated', which correctly preserves optionality.

claims.claim_text: A service entry sheet under a multi-level release procedure counts as accepted only after the last release point approves.
claims.evidence_quote: The document is not regarded as accepted until the last release point has released it.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, in the context of release procedures with successive release points.
claims.notes: Relevant to timing of service cost recognition under multi-level approval.

claims.claim_text: Service invoice verification compares the accepted entry sheet value with the invoice value and warns if the entry sheet value is exceeded.
claims.evidence_quote: If the value in the entry sheet is exceeded, the system issues a warning message.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. Comparison half carried by 'This involves comparing the value from the accepted entry sheet with that shown in the invoice and checking that the tax amounts are correct.' Note it is a WARNING, not a hard block.
claims.notes: Three-way match on services is advisory at this control point. A design that assumes a hard stop would over-constrain.

claims.claim_text: Cumulative actual values for services performed are continually updated in the underlying purchase order during performance.
claims.evidence_quote: the cumulative " actual" values (for the services actually performed) are continually updated in the underlying purchase order
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim including the stray space inside the quotation marks: 'the cumulative " actual" values (for the services actually performed) are continually updated in the underlying purchase order (standard PO or contract release order)'.
claims.notes: Supports progress tracking on the PO itself. Does NOT state that acceptance reduces commitment - consistent with the lane's honest gap note on that causal link, which I re-checked and confirm is still unsourced.

claims.claim_text: All movements of materials held as project stock pass through project stock using MM movement types with special stock indicator Q.
claims.evidence_quote: You post such movements using MM movement types, with special stock indicator Q.
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'All material movements relating to materials managed as project stock pass through project stock. You post such movements using MM movement types, with special stock indicator Q.'

claims.claim_text: A material component entered with negative quantity represents an issue of material from the network activity back into project stock.
claims.evidence_quote: Material components with a negative quantity represent issues of material from the network activity to stock.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim in a Note, followed by 'The material is delivered to project stock.'
claims.notes: Negative component quantity = return to project stock. Mechanism for material returns without a separate document type.

claims.claim_text: For project stock items the standard account assignment category is Q and the stock-bearing WBS element is the account assignment element.
claims.evidence_quote: In the standard system, account assignment category Q is used for items in purchasing documents
claims.narrower_true_statement: Both halves carried in the same Note: 'In the standard system, account assignment category Q is used for items in purchasing documents' / 'The stock-bearing WBS element acts as the account assignment element.'
claims.notes: Contrast with category F (R04-055). Q routes procurement to the stock-bearing WBS element; F routes to the order/activity.

claims.claim_text: In valuated project stock, procurement actual costs land on the WBS element and usage actual costs land on the activity.
claims.evidence_quote: actual costs from material procurement are recorded in the WBS element and those from materials usage are recorded in the activity
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim in a Note: 'In valuated project stock, actual costs from material procurement are recorded in the WBS element and those from materials usage are recorded in the activity.'
claims.notes: The procurement/usage split is the anti-double-count rule for project stock: procurement debits the WBS, usage debits the activity, so a naive roll-up that sums both against the same node WILL double-count material.

claims.claim_text: Internal activity allocation is one of the enumerated sources from which network actual costs arise.
claims.evidence_quote: Network actual costs arise from:
claims.narrower_true_statement: The quote is only the list HEADER. The list that follows is what carries the claim: 'Postings in Financial Accounting / Goods movements in Materials Management / Internal activity allocations / Overhead in cost accounting / Confirmations / Invoice receipts.'
claims.notes: WEAK QUOTE, SOUND CLAIM. The evidence_quote is a stub heading and proves nothing on its own; the six-item list immediately below it does. Recommend replacing the quote with the full list when this is cited, since a reader checking the quote alone would find no support for 'internal activity allocation'.

claims.claim_text: Plan values of appended networks raise WBS plan values, while apportioned network values raise the WBS assigned value.
claims.evidence_quote: Plan values in appended networks increase the plan values in the relevant WBS element: apportioned values increase the assigned value.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, including SAP's colon where a semicolon is meant. Preceded by 'If the activity is assigned to a WBS element, the network type and status determine whether the network is appended and/or apportioned.' Also: 'Networks flagged as preliminary planning networks (network type 21) are always appended.'
claims.notes: Appended -> plan values; apportioned -> ASSIGNED value. Since Assigned = actual + commitment (R04-035), apportioned network values compete with commitments for the same budget line. Directly relevant to anti-double-counting across the network/WBS boundary.

claims.claim_text: Internal activity allocation and assigned CO orders are among the business transactions that post actual data to the project.
claims.evidence_quote: Internal activity allocation, assigned CO orders (CO)
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim as a bullet in the list of business transactions that post actual data to the project.

claims.claim_text: Goods issue for reservations in inventory management is a documented source of project actual data.
claims.evidence_quote: Inventory Management: goods issue for reservations (MM)
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim bullet.

claims.claim_text: Costs incurred are posted directly to the WBS element, the network, or the activity according to account assignment.
claims.evidence_quote: Costs incurred are posted directly to the WBS, network, or activity.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, preceded by 'The account assignment specifies the cost object that needs to be debited for costs.'

claims.claim_text: Actual costs posted on orders attached to a project count as assigned funds for the WBS elements until settlement.
claims.evidence_quote: Although actual costs are posted to orders, they are representing assigned funds for the WBS elements.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. The 'until settlement' half is carried separately: 'During processing, the order keeps its own actual incurred costs until the costs are settled.' Also 'Based on the assigned WBS element, you can evaluate the assigned funds from orders (the planned costs, commitments, and actual costs).'
claims.notes: MAJOR DOUBLE-COUNT HAZARD, correctly captured. Order actuals appear as WBS ASSIGNED funds while simultaneously being real costs on the order. Summing order actuals and WBS assigned without eliminating the settlement leg double-counts. Note the third sentence: assigned funds from orders comprise plan, commitment AND actual - three components, not two.

claims.claim_text: A project or its work packages must be released before actual data can be entered against it.
claims.evidence_quote: You must release the project (or the work packages) before you can enter actual data.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, opening line of Project Execution.

claims.claim_text: Estimate at completion equals actual plus commitment costs already incurred plus the updated cost to complete.
claims.evidence_quote: The resulting figure is arrived at by adding the actual and commitment costs already incurred in the project to the updated cost to complete.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim: 'The resulting figure is arrived at by adding the actual and commitment costs already incurred in the project to the updated cost to complete.'
claims.notes: EAC = actual + commitment + CTC. This is the third place in the lane where actual and commitment are summed as disjoint sets (cf. Assigned in R04-035), which is the whole justification for never letting a document contribute to both.

claims.claim_text: Commitment values from periods before the forecast key date are recorded in the forecast version at the key date period.
claims.evidence_quote: Commitment values from periods before the period of the cost forecast key date are recorded in the forecast version
claims.narrower_true_statement: Full sentence: '...are recorded in the forecast version as of the period of the key date (default: current period).' Standard forecast version is CO version 110.
claims.notes: Prior-period commitments are pulled forward to the key-date period, so period-sliced commitment reporting will not tie to the forecast version without this rule.

claims.claim_text: Overhead on actual and commitment values must be calculated separately before estimating costs at completion.
claims.evidence_quote: You must calculate the overhead on actual and commitment values separately for the calculation of the estimated costs at completion.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, a prerequisite step before running the cost forecast.
claims.notes: Overhead is calculated on COMMITMENT values too, not just actuals - a commitment carries overhead. Note the new S/4HANA commitment model does not support this: 'Commitment Overhead Calculation is not supported.'

claims.claim_text: Marking an activity complete or issuing a final confirmation sets its cost to complete to zero.
claims.evidence_quote: If an activity is marked as complete or there is a final confirmation for it, the system sets the cost to complete to zero.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim.
claims.notes: Sets COST TO COMPLETE to zero - it does not say it zeroes the commitment. Distinct levers; do not conflate with ELIKZ/EREKZ.

claims.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward moves a commitment into the first period of the following fiscal year via a dedicated transaction.
claims.evidence_quote: To carry forward a commitment to the first period of the following fiscal year, proceed as follows:
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim opening line of 'Carrying Forward Commitments'. The dedicated transaction is named: KSCF, reached via Accounting > Controlling > Cost Center Accounting > Year-End Closing > Commitment Carryforward.
claims.notes: SCOPE: this topic is COST CENTER Accounting. The claim does not assert project scope, so no downgrade. The lane's gap note that project-level CJCF was never reached remains correct.

claims.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward supports a test run that computes without updating, and a reversal indicator to undo a prior carry-forward.
claims.evidence_quote: The Reversal indicator controls whether data that has already been carried forward is reversed again.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Reversal half verbatim. Test-run half carried by 'If you select Test run, the system carries forward the commitment, but does not update the results.' A third option exists: Detail Lists, which SAP advises activating together with Test run.

claims.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward moves commitments from the last period of a fiscal year to the first period of the next year.
claims.evidence_quote: You use the commitment carryforward function to carry commitments for a sales order forward from the last period of a fiscal year
claims.narrower_true_statement: The page is 'Commitment Carryforward at Year-End Closing' in Cost Object Controlling (CO-PC-OBJ), 6.0 EHP4, flagged Out of Maintenance. Every sentence on it is scoped to SALES ORDERS: 'You use the commitment carryforward function to carry commitments for a sales order forward from the last period of a fiscal year to the first period of the following year.' The Features section repeats the sales-order scope verbatim, and the worked example is 'a commitment for sales order 4711 of USD 10,000'. The page contains no general statement about commitments of any other object.
claims.notes: DOWNGRADED. NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: for SALES ORDER commitments, the carryforward function moves commitments from the last period of a fiscal year to the first period of the following year. The claim strips the sales-order qualifier and states the behaviour generally, which is exactly the product-specific-to-general generalisation the tier gate calls out. The general behaviour is separately and properly evidenced for cost centres by R04-109/110 (KSCF), so nothing is lost by tightening this record - but it must not be cited as generic proof, and note the new S/4HANA commitment model supports NO carry-forward at all.

claims.claim_text: A commitment plan pre-plans value consumption on purchase contracts, generating a plan for each contract document item.
claims.evidence_quote: You can use the commitment plan to preplan value consumption on purchase contracts.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim under Use. Per-item half carried by Result: 'A commitment plan is generated for each document item in the relevant contract. Each document item can itself have any number of items.'
claims.notes: Funds Management deliverable. Requires FM AND MM installed, configured and active - a real prerequisite, not just a switch.

claims.claim_text: Each commitment plan item generates an earmarked funds document that is copied onto referencing purchase requisitions and orders.
claims.evidence_quote: If a purchase requisition or purchase order references this contract, the earmarked funds document is copied to the purchase order
claims.narrower_true_statement: 'The system generates an earmarked funds document for a define commitment plan item' (sic, 'a define'). 'If a purchase requisition or purchase order references this contract, the earmarked funds document is copied to the purchase order and the account assignment is adopted from that document.'
claims.notes: Note the source sentence says the document is copied 'to the purchase order' even though the condition names both PR and PO. The claim's 'purchase requisitions and orders' follows the condition clause. Minor looseness in SAP's own wording, not in the claim.

claims.claim_text: Once the earmarked funds document is copied from the contract, assigning to a different account assignment object is disallowed.
claims.evidence_quote: Account assignment to a different account assignment object is then no longer allowed.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, final sentence of Result.
claims.notes: A second, independent lock on account-assignment change, distinct from the GR/IR-based lock in R04-022/048. Both must be modelled if contracts are in scope.

claims.claim_text: For projects, availability control can check against either the current budget or the released budget.
claims.evidence_quote: For projects, availability control can check against the current budget or the released budget.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, preceded by the contrast 'For internal orders, availability control checks against the current budget.' The page enumerates eight check bases (current/released x overall/annual x controlling-area/object currency), with all four released variants marked 'only for projects'.
claims.notes: This page ALSO independently defines current budget as 'Original Budget / Supplement / Return / Repostings from the Budget' - Tier-1 corroboration for R04-116, which the lane sourced only from learning.sap.com.

claims.claim_text: Current budget is the original budget together with budget supplements, budget returns, and budget transfers.
claims.evidence_quote: The _Current budget_ column displays the original budget together with the budget supplements, budget returns, and budget transfers.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Rendered page text reads 'The Current budget column displays the original budget together with the budget supplements, budget returns, and budget transfers.' The recorded quote wraps 'Current budget' in markdown underscores (_Current budget_), an artefact of the lane's markdown capture, not page text. Substantively identical; treated as matched.
claims.notes: Tier-1 corroboration exists on the budget-profile page (R04-115 source), which words the fourth element as 'Repostings from the Budget' rather than 'budget transfers'. Same concept, different label - prefer the Tier-1 wording in the deliverable.

claims.claim_text: Commitment management must be active for the controlling area and current fiscal year before commitments are recorded.
claims.evidence_quote: First, in the Controlling Area, Commitment Management must be active for the current fiscal year (transaction OKKP).
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim. The page adds the per-object prerequisites the claim omits: 'the object concerned must be able to accept commitments' - Orders: switch in the Order Type; Cost Centers: Lock indicator not set (KS03); Projects: see note 47992. Field XOBLR on EBAN/EKPO flags per-item commitment relevance, set by function ME_ACCOUNTING_CHECK.
claims.notes: Controlling-area activation is necessary but NOT sufficient - there is a second, per-object gate. Corroborated Tier-1 for projects by the new-commitment lesson ('If Commitment Management is active in the controlling area, it is also automatically active for projects') and for cost centres by the lock-indicator note.

claims.claim_text: Account assignment cannot be changed on goods receipt documents, unlike on invoices where unplanned accounts are permitted.
claims.evidence_quote: On goods receipt documents it’s not possible to change the account information.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim (curly apostrophe). Full context: 'On goods receipt documents it\'s not possible to change the account information. The sentences in EKBE (for non-service items) have the field ZEKKN = \'0\' and the quantities and values are distributed among the accounts in a progressive fill-up way.' The invoice contrast is carried by section 8.1: 'On invoices documents it\'s possible to change the account provided.'
claims.notes: Note the second sentence: GR values against a MULTI-account PO are distributed progressive fill-up, with no option to choose proportional. That asymmetry versus invoices (where TWRKZ offers both) is design-relevant and is not captured by any record in the lane.

claims.claim_text: A dedicated routine checks on every purchase order change whether anything commitment-relevant has changed before re-sending to accounting.
claims.evidence_quote: It also check when a PO has been changed if something relevant for the commitments has been changed.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, under FORM RKO_STATISTICS: 'This routine checks whether the PO item are commitment relevant or not. It also check when a PO has been changed if something relevant for the commitments has been changed.' Dispatch is via function RWIN_CHECK against table TRWIN/TRWPR.
claims.notes: Supports an event-driven change-detection design, but the source does NOT enumerate WHICH fields are commitment-relevant. The lane's gap note on PO amendment recalculation stands: the recalculation rule must be designed, not copied.

claims.claim_text: The PO communication structure must always carry both purchase order and receipt/invoice quantities and values, regardless of the triggering event.
claims.evidence_quote: the purchasing quantities and values and the goods receipt quantities and values are also relevant and should be correctly available
claims.narrower_true_statement: Quote verbatim. The general principle is stated immediately before it: 'On the communication structures (EKBP / EKPR) all information regarding the purchasing document should always be provided to the financial areas, independently from the event.'
claims.notes: STRONGEST ARCHITECTURAL LESSON IN THE LANE for anti-double-counting: SAP does not send deltas. Every event resends the FULL current picture (PO values/quantities plus cumulative GR and IR values/quantities) and lets the financial side recompute open = purchased - reduced. An idempotent full-restatement interface is inherently immune to double-counting on retry or replay; a delta/increment interface is not.

claims.claim_text: When the GR indicator is not set on the purchase order item, the commitment is reduced when invoices are received.
claims.evidence_quote: GR Indicator is not set: Commitment is reduced when invoices are received.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, including SAP's inconsistent capitalisation ('GR Indicator is not set' versus 'GR indicator set' in the preceding line).
claims.notes: Together with R04-025 this is the Tier-1 two-line rule. See contradictions[0] for why it is necessary but not sufficient.

claims.claim_text: The Assigned column on a project budget view only appears when availability control is active for the project.
claims.evidence_quote: The _Assigned_ column only displays if the availability control is active for the project.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Rendered text: 'The Assigned column only displays if the availability control is active for the project.' Same markdown-underscore artefact as R04-116; substantively identical.
claims.notes: Assigned (= actual + commitment) is not merely a report column but is gated on availability control being active - so switching AVAC off silently removes the anti-double-count view.

claims.claim_text: If budget releases are used, availability control must run against the released budget rather than the current budget.
claims.evidence_quote: If you work with budget releases, you need to also perform availability control against the released budget and not against the current budget.
claims.narrower_true_statement: Verbatim, in a Caution block. Context: 'Budget release means that you release the current budget in stages so that available funds are not exhausted at an early stage. Releasing the budget is optional.' Also 'The budget release has nothing to do with setting the Released status at WBS element level.'

claims.narrower_true_statement: The cited page is an SAP Fiori ELEMENTS framework article. Its full text reads: 'With SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar and shares many features and settings with the list report...' It then gives only a feature-availability table (view management, header title, filter bar unavailable, table title with row count, growing table, search in table toolbar, personalization, export). The words 'comparably small', 'one by one', and 'predefined' appear NOWHERE on this page. The page itself defers design intent elsewhere: 'For design information, see the Worklist Floorplan guidelines' - the article the lane's own gaps note proves is absent from the published index.
claims.notes: TWO problems. (1) SCOPE: the source states a framework-specific behaviour ('With SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is...'); the claim generalises it into a floorplan-wide definition. (2) UNSOURCED ADDITIONS: 'processing a predefined, comparably small set of items one by one' is not on this page. 'Predefined set of objects' is sourced, but from a DIFFERENT page (when-to-use-which-floorplan, the source of R08-051). 'Comparably small' and 'one by one' are supported by NEITHER page. Narrower true statement: in SAP Fiori elements, the worklist is a simplified list report without a filter bar; per when-to-use-which-floorplan it is for processing a predefined set of objects where a filter bar is not needed and predefined views are possible. Load this claim into the blueprint WITHOUT any size ceiling.
